subject: history_social
passage: After 1803, when forces of the East India Company took Delhi, the Mughal emperor continued to reside in the Red Fort, to receive the ceremonial respects of visiting dignitaries, and to confer titles that ambitious men still thought worth having. Coins struck by the Company itself bore his name until 1835, and prayers in the city's mosques were said in it. Yet the revenues of his former provinces went elsewhere, his court was paid an allowance by the Company, and no order he issued had force beyond the walls of his palace. Historians describing the half century that followed therefore distinguish carefully between the emperor's ______ sovereignty, which the Company found convenient to preserve, and the real authority that it had long since taken for itself.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: The sentence contrasts the emperor's sovereignty with "the real authority" held by the Company. The text has shown that the emperor kept the titles and ceremonies of rule while "no order he issued had force beyond the walls of his palace." Sovereignty that exists in name but not in fact is "nominal."
explanation.A: Incorrect. The emperor's position was inherited, but "hereditary" does not contrast with "real authority," which is the distinction the sentence draws.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Absolute" means unlimited. The emperor's orders had no force beyond his palace walls, so his sovereignty was the opposite of unlimited.
explanation.C: Correct. "Nominal" means existing in name only, which fits an emperor whose name appeared on coins and in prayers while the Company held the real power.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Contested" means disputed. No one disputed the emperor's title; the Company "found it convenient to preserve." The point is that the title was empty, not that it was challenged.
